abstract: Maillard reaction products contribute to flavor formation and flavor-enhancing effects during food processing; however, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. We previously identified 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (5-HMF), a major Maillard reaction intermediate, in heated shio-koji lees and showed that it prolongs the umami aftertaste. We investigated its effect on the calcium-sensing receptor (CaSR), implicated in kokumi perception, and the umami taste receptors T1R1/T1R3. We found that 5-HMF elicited concentration-dependent intracellular Ca2+ responses in CaSR-expressing cells, but not in T1R1/T1R3-expressing cells. The CaSR responded to the structural analogs of 5-HMF, furfural, and 5-methylfurfural (5-MF), whereas furfuryl alcohol elicited no significant response, suggesting that the furan-2-carbaldehyde moiety primarily drives CaSR recognition. The CaSR-selective antagonist, NPS-2143, suppressed the response to 5-HMF and furfural. These compounds potentiated CaSR concentration responses to extracellular Ca2+, indicating their function as positive allosteric modulators. These findings reveal a molecular basis for kokumi perception elicited by Maillard reaction products.
